step_goal: Compile guide-backed opening-hand expectations into a syntax-safe HearthRanger VisionAI `Mulligan.json` that preserves aggressive keep intent, documented discard intent, documented selector syntax, and explicit suppression of unsupported or non-runtime-safe conditions.
required_inputs: A normalized mulligan contract with `default_keep`, `conditional_keep`, `default_throw`, stable `rule_id` values, and source references.
Resolved Hearthstone CardIDs for every concrete card selector that may appear in `mulligan` rows.
Optional matchup metadata that explicitly tags coin-only, no-coin-only, and opponent-class-specific claims.
A compiler capability matrix that separates officially documented Mulligan syntax from the narrower repo-approved runtime-safe condition subset.
An ordered rule list so emitted rows preserve intended priority instead of re-sorting by card or condition.
produced_outputs: A runtime-target `Mulligan.json` file with `GameCardId`, `ConfigComment`, and `Mulligan.values` rows.
A `mulligan_condition_suppression_report.json` artifact that records every guide condition that was intentionally not emitted to runtime.
A `mulligan_compilation_receipt.json` or equivalent embedded receipt that records source refs, rule order, suppressions, and validation results.
Per-row provenance entries that map each emitted Mulligan row back to a stable gameplan rule and source citation.
reliable_uses: Emit syntactically valid Mulligan rows with the required row keys `comment`, `mulligan`, `condition`, and `value`.
Compile unconditional keeps and throws into `condition: "*"` rows using concrete CardIDs or documented `DROPn` selectors.
Compile documented same-hand synergy selectors such as `CARD_A + CARD_B` and `DROP1 + CARD_A` when the guide claim is concrete enough.

Compile duplicated-card keeps with the documented comma-plus selector form when the runtime version requirement is acceptable, for example `LOOT_149, LOOT_149+ LOOT_149` for version 10.4.5.0 or higher.
Compile `coin` and `nocoin` branches when the guide claim maps directly to the official Mulligan condition surface.
Compile opponent-class branches when the condition uses documented hero checks such as `opp_hero(count(),warrior=true) > 0` or `hero_class=warrior | rogue | paladin`.
Preserve aggressive keep intent by using broad documented selectors like `DROP1`, `DROP2`, `DROP3`, and plus-combos instead of collapsing everything to single-card keeps.
Suppress guide clauses that require unsupported or locally unvalidated Mulligan predicates instead of forcing them into runtime JSON.
limitations: This step can compile documented Mulligan syntax, but it cannot prove that the resulting rules improve gameplay or that HearthRanger actually loaded them in a live runtime session.
This step must not invent undocumented Mulligan grammar for vague guide advice such as `keep if curve is good`, `keep if enough early pressure`, or `keep if spell density is high`.

The current repo preview validator intentionally allows a narrower Mulligan condition subset than the broader generic VisionAI condition language, so some officially documented-looking guide translations must still be suppressed for local runtime safety.

The official Mulligan page explicitly documents that hold beats discard, but it does not explicitly document same-type tie-break behavior for overlapping hold rows or overlapping discard rows, so preserving author order is a conservative policy rather than a proven runtime rule [uncertain].
relevant_config_surfaces: `CustomConfig/deck_config.ini` `[CONFIGS]` mapping from exact deck name to config directory.
`CustomConfig/<deck>/Mulligan.json` as the runtime surface for opening-hand rules.
The HSConfig gameplan surface that feeds this step, typically `mulligan_plan.default_keep`, `mulligan_plan.conditional_keep`, and `mulligan_plan.default_throw`.
aggressive_generation_policy: Default to the most aggressive documented keep expression that the guide actually supports, preferring `DROPn` selectors or plus-combos when they describe the guide better than isolated single-card rows.
Emit explicit discard rows for guide-backed throws, but keep any overlapping documented hold rows because the official Mulligan doc states that hold has higher priority than discard.
Preserve ordered rule emission from the normalized gameplan instead of alphabetizing rows, so the compiler does not accidentally change priority intent.
Translate coin and no-coin advice only into the documented `coin`, `nocoin`, or opening-hand-count equivalents shown in the official Mulligan doc.
Translate matchup advice only when it can be expressed with official opponent-hero patterns; otherwise keep the richer guide clause in the gameplan contract and emit a suppression report entry.

Do not downgrade aggressive guide clauses into timid single-card keeps just to avoid suppression; prefer exact documented selectors first, then suppress with an explanation if no documented selector can carry the claim.

Treat unsupported composite guide logic such as `coin OR cheap curve in hand` as report-only unless a separate compiler pass can split it into multiple individually documented rows without changing meaning.
validation_gates: The research result must cover every required field from `fields.yaml` and pass `validate_json.py` for this research batch.
Generated `Mulligan.json` must be strict JSON with no comments or trailing commas.
Top-level Mulligan structure must be exactly `GameCardId`, `ConfigComment`, and `Mulligan`.
Every emitted Mulligan row must contain `comment`, `mulligan`, `condition`, and `value`, and `value` must be either `hold` or `discard`.

Every emitted `condition` must pass the local runtime-safety gate used by `hsranger_core.mulligan_runtime_safety.runtime_safe_mulligan_condition` when the target is the current preview/apply workflow.
Every emitted row must have exactly one provenance mapping back to a stable gameplan rule and documented source surface.
Every suppressed guide condition must appear in `mulligan_condition_suppression_report.json` with the raw condition text and the suppression reason.
architectural_implications: HSConfig should implement a dedicated Mulligan compiler instead of treating Mulligan rows as generic JSON text templates.
That compiler should have separate sub-stages for selector compilation, condition compilation, row ordering, and suppression reporting.
Selector compilation should understand concrete CardIDs, `DROPn`, documented plus-combos, and the duplicated-card selector form.
Condition compilation should operate in two modes: an official-doc understanding mode and a stricter runtime-safe emission mode for the current HSranger preview pipeline.

The current repo files `src/hsranger_core/config_author.py`, `src/hsranger_core/mulligan_runtime_safety.py`, and `src/hsranger_core/visionai_model.py` already define the enforcement boundary that HSConfig should target for preview-safe output.
HSConfig should keep unsupported guide richness in its own machine-readable contract instead of flattening or silently discarding it, then expose a suppression report for operator review.
Priority must be modeled explicitly because `hold` versus `discard` precedence is part of the official contract, and row order should remain stable across rebuilds for diffability.
recommended_contracts: A `mulligan_plan` contract with `rule_id`, `default_keep`, `conditional_keep`, `default_throw`, `source_refs`, and explicit per-claim condition metadata.

A `mulligan_compiler_capabilities.json` contract that lists allowed selectors, allowed condition families, version-gated features such as `hero_class` and duplicate-selector syntax, and suppression reasons.
A `mulligan_row_provenance` contract that records file path, JSON pointer, source doc key, source gameplan key, confidence, and patchability.
A `mulligan_condition_suppression_report.json` contract with `status`, `suppressed_count`, `suppressed_condition_keys`, `items`, `raw_condition`, and human-readable suppression reasons.
A `mulligan_compilation_receipt.json` contract that records emitted row order, source URLs, validator status, and version assumptions.
never_autogenerate_without: Official HearthRanger Mulligan documentation and generic JSON-condition documentation cited in the compilation receipt.
Concrete CardID resolution for every emitted non-`DROPn` selector.
An explicit ordered mulligan plan rather than an unordered set of keep suggestions.
A documented translation path for every emitted condition, or a suppression report entry when no safe translation exists.
A successful local syntax and runtime-safety validation pass for the emitted Mulligan rows.
A declared version floor when using documented version-gated features such as `hero_class` or the duplicate-selector sample.
